Task reviewer: Spec ✅ - all requirements met, nothing extra.
  Strengths: Good test coverage, clean. Issues: None. Task quality: Approved.

[Ledger: Task 1: complete (commits a1b2c3d..d4e5f6a, review clean)]

Task 2: Recovery modes

[Run task-brief for Task 2; dispatch implementer with brief + report paths + context]

Implementer: [No questions]
  - Added verify/repair modes
  - 8/8 tests passing
  - Committed

[Run review-package PLAN_FILE BASE HEAD; dispatch task reviewer with the printed path]
Task reviewer: Spec ❌:
  - Missing: Progress reporting (spec says "report every 100 items")

re-reviewer verifies the findings were addressed and checks the fix diff for
new breakage. It is not a fresh review — the full review already happened.

**Purpose:** Verify each finding from the previous review was addressed, and
that the fix itself broke nothing.

```

    You are re-reviewing one task's fix round. A previous review produced

    `git diff --stat [FIX_BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]` and
    `git diff [FIX_BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]`.

    Your review is read-only on this checkout. Do not mutate the working
    tree, the index, HEAD, or branch state in any way.

    ## Scope

    Your scope is the findings list and the fix diff. Verdict every finding.
    Inspect the fix diff for new problems the fix itself introduced. Do NOT
    re-review code the fix did not touch: if you notice an issue entirely

Task review is back. The security-critical part passed on its merits — the reviewer traced tenant scoping by hand across all seven queries, both id-provenance paths in `getReceipts`, the `$or`/`currentlyValidFilter` interaction, the anchor-kind dispatch, and both `Promise.all` destructurings, and found no cross-tenant path. Your three deviations were each verified as correct and necessary. Good work.

One **Important** finding to fix.

## `list-briefs.ts` sends entire untruncated source bodies to the client

`buildBrief` renders a raw-source line as `source.excerpt ?? source.content ?? ""` (`packages/knowledge/brief.ts:87`). But `excerpt` only exists on `$project`ed search hits — `$substrCP` at 1500 chars in `packages/knowledge/search.ts:182`. The `Source` **schema has no `excerpt` field at all** (`packages/knowledge/schemas/sources.ts`). `listBriefs` fetches whole documents with a plain `.find()` and no projection, so `excerpt` is always `undefined` and every raw-source brief line falls through to `content` — the complete email body or voice transcript.

Concretely: a forwarded 40 KB email thread lands unreviewed, and the brief card renders a `BriefLine.text` containing all 40 KB, serialized into the client payload on every page load. The receipt path clamps the same content to 280 chars (`packages/knowledge/receipt.ts`), which is the budget this was supposed to respect.

The `as ReceiptSource` cast at `list-briefs.ts:120` is what makes the mismatch invisible — `Source` is structurally assignable to `ReceiptSource` without it, so the cast buys nothing and silences exactly this class of error.

**Fix, three parts:**

1. Give sources a real `excerpt` before handing them to `buildBrief`. Use **280** — the same `PREVIEW_LENGTH` the receipt uses — rather than inventing a third number. A brief line is a one-line card; it should never be longer than the receipt that explains it. If `PREVIEW_LENGTH` is not exported from `@repo/knowledge`, export it rather than duplicating the literal.
2. Drop the `as ReceiptSource` casts at `list-briefs.ts:120` and `get-receipts.ts:70` if the code compiles without them. If either genuinely needs one, keep it and say in your report what the real type mismatch is.
3. The query at `list-briefs.ts:76-80` pulls 20 whole documents — content, audio blob URLs, attachments — to use at most 2. Add a projection so it fetches only the fields `ReceiptSource` actually needs.

Then: `cd apps/app && bunx tsc --noEmit`, run `bun test`, append a fix report to your report file (what you changed, the commands, the output), and reply with the short status contract.

**Do not act on these** — eight Minor findings were recorded and deliberately deferred for the final whole-branch review: the lowercase-fixture mutant gap in `member-names.test.ts`, duplicate receipts from repeated `sourceIds`, no runtime shape validation on the action input, the unbounded facts load, the non-defensive `ANCHOR_ID` lookup, the "freshest anchor" comment being about review-time rather than capture-time recency, and a stale comment in `collections.ts` naming a `listBriefTargets` function that no longer exists.

No duplicated literal.

  - Predicate parity: `$match` filter (`status: { $ne: "reviewed" }, tenantId: orgId`), `$sort: { createdAt: -1 }`, and `$limit: RAW_SOURCE_SCAN` are byte-for-byte the same predicate/sort/limit the removed `.find()` used — confirmed against the diff's unchanged context lines. No tenant-scoping regression.
  - Projection completeness: `$project` emits `capturedBy`, `createdAt`, `email.subject`, `excerpt` (computed), `occurredAt`, `status`, `type`, plus implicit `_id`. Checked every field `ReceiptSource` (packages/knowledge/receipt.ts:42-52) requires/reads via `provenanceRow`/`quoteOf`/`sourceReceipt` — all present. `content`, `attachments`, `audio` are correctly omitted (that's the point of the fix).

This is not Critical: an untranscribed voice source will not crash `listBriefs`; it degrades to an empty `excerpt` string, which `buildBrief`'s `source.excerpt ?? source.content ?? ""` accepts safely (excerpt is now always a defined string, so it always wins the `??` chain — `content` is never reached, which is intended since `content` isn't even projected).

None found. The pipeline change is scoped, predicate-preserving, and typechecks cleanly (verified independently). The `$substrCP`-on-missing-content path was the one real risk named in the review brief and it resolves safely (empty string, no throw).

**Out-of-Scope Observations**

- `apps/app/app/actions/knowledge/get-receipts.ts:57-62` — the `sources.find(...)` query there still fetches whole `Source` documents (content, attachments, audio URLs) with no projection, i.e. the same DB-round-trip weight the original finding complained about, just on a different query. This is legitimately out of scope: the finding's part 3 named `list-briefs.ts:120`/"20 whole documents" specifically (matching `RAW_SOURCE_SCAN`), not `get-receipts.ts`. No client-facing leak results — `composeReceipt`'s `quoteOf` truncates to `PREVIEW_LENGTH` before the `Receipt` is returned — so this is a performance-only observation, not a privacy regression. The implementer flagged it explicitly in the fix report as a candidate for a future pass. Non-blocking.

**Fix round:** All findings addressed, no new Critical/Important breakage.

The agent's instructions already require it to surface conflicts rather than silently pick a winner — but it has never had any way to know a conflict exists. This adds one boolean per fact so it can.

This is a small, surgical change. Do not restructure the file.

## What earlier tasks built

`findContestedFactIds(db, tenantId, factIds: ObjectId[]): Promise<Set<string>>` is exported from `@repo/knowledge` (the barrel). It takes ObjectIds and returns a Set of hex strings. It filters on `tenantId` and on open contradiction proposals only.

## Global constraints that bind this task

- **Do not touch `apps/app/agent/instructions.md`.** Nine eval suites depend on its wording and on the `<fact id="…"/>` / `<source id="…"/>` citation protocol. This change is purely additive to the tool's return value.
